en.g: a female given name from Norwegian; a variant of Ena

1001769.etyen:
Variant of Ena (“female given name”). The ultimate origin is therefore uncertain, since several etymologies have been proposed for Ena.
One possibility derives the name through Irish Eithne (“female given name”), from Middle Irish Eithne, from Old Irish Eithne. The name has traditionally been associated with Irish eithne (“kernel”), from Middle Irish eitne (“grain, kernel”), ultimately from *h₁ét(e)no- (“kernel”).
A second possibility is that Ena originated as a short form of female given names ending in -ena or -ene.

Lexicalized genitive of farken (“the devil, hell; damn”), an alteration of fanden (“the Devil; damn”), under the influence of fark (“vagrant, rogue”).
Fanden is from Old Norse fendinn (“the Devil”), probably from Old Frisian fandiand (“tempter”), the present participle of fandia (“to tempt”), from *fandōną (“to seek, search for, examine”), ultimately related to the Proto-Indo-European root *pent- (“to pass; path”). Because this branch beyond Old Norse is probable rather than certain, it is not used for categorical derivation here.
